title: Long video and memory: chunks, tiled decode, and what truly helps
hook: Tiled decode can't save a sampler that's out of memory, and H3 ignores it anyway. Match each fix to the cost it really touches.

verified.claim: Sampler memory is estimated from the latent's area and a per-model factor, and no decode setting appears in it.
LTX's decode estimate counts T, H and W. Wan 2.2's has no T. H3's clamps to one chunk.
A tiled decode's memory estimate is the estimate for one tile.
H3's decode_tiled calls decode, and its tile settings are ignored.
e_chain_join validates and runs on a CPU, and writes 17 frames from 9 + 8.
The gallery short film has 544 frames, and H3 shots have 124.

unchecked: The memory numbers are ComfyUI's own estimates, used to plan loading. They are not measured peaks, and comments in the code call parts of them rough.
The notes on chained clips and on context windows are from our earlier studio's records, on another software stack. Treat them as leads. We did not rerun them.
We did not measure how visible seams are for any overlap. The lab counts work only.
Whether the attention pairs in the table match real memory depends on the attention code. Real models may window or batch; the number is a count, not a measurement.
